claims.text: Wear resistance of the FeNiCrCoCu thin coating during high-temperature sliding is governed by the formation and evolution of a nanocrystalline surface layer.
Microscopic deformation of the FeNiCrCoCu thin coating during high-temperature sliding is governed by the formation and evolution of a nanocrystalline surface layer.
The nanocrystalline surface layer acts as a sacrificial layer.
The nanocrystalline surface layer absorbs and dissipates energy generated by sliding contact.
Using in-situ TEM or AFM during sliding will produce a 20–50% reduction in wear rate relative to a coating tested without in-situ TEM or AFM characterization.
Using in-situ TEM or AFM during sliding will produce a 10–30% reduction in microscopic deformation relative to a coating tested without in-situ TEM or AFM characterization.
The predicted behavior is expected at 500–700°C.
The predicted behavior is expected at sliding speeds of 0.1–1 m/s.
The predicted behavior is expected under normal loads of 10–50 N.
Coating thickness may affect wear resistance and microscopic deformation.
Substrate material may affect wear resistance and microscopic deformation.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis attributes performance to a nanocrystalline surface layer, but the nominal controlled change is the presence of in-situ TEM or AFM characterization. Characterization is presented as causing improved wear and deformation even though no material or processing change is specified that would alter formation of the proposed layer.
